title: Criterion for K-injectivity
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a Grothendieck abelian category [def-sp-grothendieck-abelian] and $\kappa$ a cardinal. For an object $M$ of $\mathcal A$ its *size* $|M|$ is the cardinality of the set of subobjects of $M$. Assume that for every acyclic (as in [def-pc-acyclic-complex-modules] with $\mathcal A$ in place of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$) cochain complex $M^\bullet$ in $\mathcal A$ (cochain complexes defined as in [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] with $\mathcal A$ in place of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$): (a) if $M^\bullet\neq0$, there is a nonzero bounded-above acyclic subcomplex $N^\bullet\subset M^\bullet$ with $|N^n|\le\kappa$ for all $n$; (b) there is a surjection of complexes $\bigoplus_{i\in I}M_i^\bullet\to M^\bullet$ with each $M_i^\bullet$ bounded above, acyclic, and $|M_i^n|\le\kappa$ for all $n$. Let $I^\bullet$ be a cochain complex in $\mathcal A$ such that (1) each $I^j$ is an injective object [def-sp-injective-resolutions], and (2) for every bounded-above acyclic complex $M^\bullet$ with $|M^n|\le\kappa$ for all $n$, every morphism of complexes $M^\bullet\to I^\bullet$ is homotopic to zero. Then $I^\bullet$ is K-injective (as in [def-pur-kinjective-complex] with $\mathcal A$ in place of $\Mod(\mathcal O)$).

proof.text: Let $M^\bullet$ be any acyclic complex. By transfinite recursion construct acyclic subcomplexes $K_\alpha^\bullet\subset M^\bullet$: set $K_0^\bullet=0$; at a successor $\alpha=\beta+1$, if $K_\beta^\bullet=M^\bullet$ keep it unchanged, and otherwise apply assumption (a) in the statement to the nonzero acyclic quotient $M^\bullet/K_\beta^\bullet$ and take the inverse image of the resulting nonzero bounded-above acyclic subcomplex; at a limit ordinal take the colimit of the earlier subcomplexes. The inverse image is acyclic because it is an extension of acyclic complexes, filtered colimits preserve exactness in a Grothendieck category, and a strictly increasing chain of subobjects of the set of subobjects of each $M^n$ cannot continue indefinitely. Thus the process reaches $M^\bullet$ at some ordinal.

source.place: Lemma lemma-characterize-K-injective, proof: transfinite construction of K_alpha

proof.text: We prove by transfinite induction, simultaneously for every $n\in\mathbb Z$, that $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(K_\alpha^\bullet[n],I^\bullet)=0$. The assertion is immediate for $K_0^\bullet=0$. At a successor where the chain has already reached $M^\bullet$ it is unchanged. Otherwise there is a short exact sequence $0\to K_\beta^\bullet\to K_{\beta+1}^\bullet\to N_{\beta+1}^\bullet\to0$ with $N_{\beta+1}^\bullet$ bounded above, acyclic, and termwise of size at most $\kappa$. Shifting this sequence by $n$ and applying [lem-pur-kinjective-homotopy-exact-injective-target] with target $I^\bullet$ gives an exact Hom sequence. The left term vanishes by induction. The right term vanishes by hypothesis (2) applied to the shifted bounded-above acyclic complex $N_{\beta+1}^\bullet[n]$, whose term sizes are unchanged. Hence the middle term vanishes for every $n$.

At a limit ordinal $\lambda$, the Hom complexes $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K_\lambda^\bullet,I^\bullet)$ are the inverse limit of the Hom complexes $\operatorname{Hom}^\bullet(K_\beta^\bullet,I^\bullet)$, and their transition maps are surjective because every term of $I^\bullet$ is injective. Therefore [lem-pur-kinjective-homotopy-limit-vanishing] applies: the induction hypothesis gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(K_\beta^\bullet[n],I^\bullet)=0$ for every earlier $\beta$ and every shift $n$, so it gives the same conclusion for $K_\lambda^\bullet$.

source.place: Lemma lemma-characterize-K-injective, proof: limit step using Homology Lemma homology-lemma-ML-over-ordinals

proof.text: Choose an ordinal at which the construction has reached $M^\bullet$. The preceding induction gives $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(M^\bullet,I^\bullet[n])=0$ for every $n$, so in particular the case $n=0$ says $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(\mathcal A)}(M^\bullet,I^\bullet)=0$. By [def-pur-kinjective-complex] this is equivalent to every morphism from the acyclic complex $M^\bullet$ to $I^\bullet$ being homotopic to zero. Since $M^\bullet$ was arbitrary, $I^\bullet$ is K-injective.
